# Exact Weighted Interpolation and a Soundness-Score Obstruction at (p,d)=(147457,87)

## Abstract

For the affine line-versus-point test over $F_{147457}^2$ with total degree $87$, I replace the coarse weighted-monomial estimate in the published KTZ chain by an exact count. At the smallest selected-line cardinality permitted by KTZ Lemma 3.2, namely $100(p+1)=14,745,800$, the published safe choice is $D=573,088>p$. Exact counting instead certifies $D=87,668<p$, with a linear-system surplus of $20,520,648$ dimensions. This yields a nonzero squarefree explainer with nonzero $Z$-derivative for arbitrary line labels and arbitrary direction concentration.

Two adversarial findings prevent this from becoming a meaningful end-to-end improvement. First, later printed KTZ inequalities remain impossible at this fixed field. Second, the campaign score itself has a constant-polynomial floor: every point table has agreement at least $1/p$, so arbitrarily small epsilon values are formally sound. I record the exact terminating value $epsilon_*=10^{-6}$, with required agreement $10^{-7}$, only to expose this defect. Conversely, an exact probabilistic construction gives tables with pass probability at least $88/p$ and global degree-87 agreement below $2/p$, refuting $epsilon=20/p$.

The active corpus contained no prior submission, no verifier audit, no lemma-book entry, and no promoted result at the final snapshot. Thus the comparison threshold is the configured sentinel $1$, not a doubly verified theorem.

## Test and Notation

Set

- $p=147457$,
- $d=87$,
- $m=2$,
- $epsilon_*=10^{-6}=1/1,000,000$,
- $r_0=100(p+1)=14,745,800$,
- $D=87,668$,
- interpolation multiplicity $s=1$.

There are $p(p+1)$ affine lines. Sampling a uniformly random line and then a uniformly random point on it is the uniform distribution on the $p^2(p+1)$ incident point-line pairs.

For $A in F_p[X,Y,Z]$, define

$$wdeg(A)=max\{i+j+87k:[X^iY^jZ^k]A ne 0\}.$$

Let $V_D$ be spanned by monomials $X^iY^jZ^k$ with $i+j+87k<=D$ and with $k=0$ or $p$ not dividing $k$. Since $D=87,668$ gives $k<=1007<p$, no exponent is deleted and

$$N(D):=dim V_D=sum_{k=0}^{floor(D/87)} {D-87k+2 choose 2}.$$

## Prior Results

[KTZ revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download), Theorem 1.1, studies precisely uniform incident-pair sampling and total degree. Its bivariate proof ends with agreement $epsilon/8000$, not the required $epsilon/10$. Lemma 3.2 requires the selected family to have measure at least $100/p$, hence cardinality at least $r_0$. Section 4 chooses

$$D_{KTZ}=16(floor(sqrt{87|R|})+1).$$

At $|R|=r_0$, this is $573,088>p$. Lemma 4.1 also requires $D<k_1/2$, where $k_1=floor(epsilon p/1000)$, and requires $1/sqrt{p+1}<=epsilon/8000$.

[HKSS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.12752v1), Lemma A.7, uses the same linear-algebra condition $|N_{d,D,p}|>r(D+1)$. Claim A.4 supplies a purported cubic estimate, Claims A.5--A.6 remove inseparable $Z$-exponents, and Theorem 4.3 uses the resulting interpolant. The exact calculation below shows that Claim A.4 is false as printed. The coarser Claim A.6 needed for interpolation is independently repairable and is not assumed here.

No theorem from Arora--Sudan, no higher-dimensional lift, and no extension-field descent is used.

## Theorem

**Lemma 1 (fixed-instance weighted interpolation).** Let $R$ be a set of at most $14,745,800$ distinct affine lines in $F_{147457}^2$. For every assignment to each $L in R$ of a polynomial $p_L in F_{147457}[t]$ of degree at most $87$ relative to an affine parametrization $L(t)$, there is a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A in F_{147457}[X,Y,Z]$ such that $wdeg(A)<=87,668$, $A_Z ne 0$, and $A(L(t),p_L(t))=0$ in $F_{147457}[t]$ for every $L in R$.

**Theorem 2 (formal score and obstruction).** For every point table $f$ and line table $P$, if $Pass(f,P)>=10^{-6}$, then a total-degree-at-most-$87$ polynomial agrees with $f$ on at least $10^{-7}$ of $F_{147457}^2$. There exist a point table $f$ and degree-at-most-$87$ line table $P$ such that $Pass(f,P)>=88/147457$ and $Agr_{87}(f)<2/147457$.

## Proof

**[P1, proved] Exact monomial count.** Since $87,668=87*1007+59$, reversing the summation index gives

$$N(87,668)=sum_{j=0}^{1007}{87j+61 choose 2}.$$

Using

$$sum 1=1008, quad sum j=507,528, quad sum j^2=340,889,640,$$

we obtain the checkable integer certificate

$$
N(87,668)
=frac{7569(340,889,640)+10,527(507,528)+3660(1008)}2
=1,292,770,060,848.
$$

Each identity $A(L(t),p_L(t))=0$ has degree at most $D$ in $t$ and therefore imposes at most $D+1=87,669$ homogeneous linear conditions. At $r_0$ lines the number of conditions is at most

$$14,745,800*87,669=1,292,749,540,200.$$

The coefficient surplus is exactly $20,520,648$.

**[P2, proved] Interpolation.** If $|R|<r_0$, augment $R$ to $r_0$ distinct affine lines and give each new line an arbitrary degree-at-most-87 label. This is possible because $p(p+1)=21,743,714,306>r_0$. Apply the restriction map from $V_D$ to $r_0$ copies of the space of univariate polynomials of degree at most $D$. By [P1], its kernel has dimension at least $20,520,648$. A nonzero kernel element gives all required formal identities; restricting back to the original family loses nothing.

**[P3, proved] Nonzero derivative.** A kernel element independent of $Z$ would be a nonzero bivariate polynomial of total degree at most $87,668$ vanishing identically on $r_0$ distinct affine lines. The defining linear polynomial of each line would divide it. Their product has degree $r_0>87,668$, a contradiction. Thus the interpolant depends on $Z$. Every positive $Z$-exponent is in $\{1,...,1007\}$ and is nonzero modulo $p$, so formal differentiation in $Z$ cannot annihilate it.

**[P4, proved] Squarefree cleanup.** Choose a valid interpolant with nonzero $Z$-derivative and minimum weighted degree. Suppose $A=F^eG$, where $F$ is irreducible, $e>=2$, and $F$ does not divide $G$. On every line graph, $F_L^eG_L=0$ in the integral domain $F_p[t]$, hence $F_LG_L=0$; therefore $FG$ remains an interpolant. If $(FG)_Z=0$, reduction modulo $F$ gives $F|F_ZG$, hence $F|F_Z$. Since $deg_Z(F_Z)<deg_Z(F)$ unless $F_Z=0$, one gets $F_Z=0$, then $G_Z=0$, and consequently $A_Z=0$, a contradiction. Thus $(FG)_Z ne0$, while $wdeg(FG)<wdeg(A)$, contradicting minimality. Hence $A$ is squarefree.

**[P5, proved] Degree cutoff for this counting method.** At $D=87,667$,

$$N(D)=1,292,725,845,432,$$

whereas

$$r_0(D+1)=14,745,800*87,668=1,292,734,794,400.$$

The deficit is $8,948,968$. The number of monomials of exact weighted degree $s$ is nondecreasing in $s$, so $N(D)/(D+1)$ is nondecreasing. Hence no smaller $D$ satisfies the universal dimension inequality. This proves that $87,668$ is the first degree certified by this coefficient-count method, not that smaller interpolants never exist for special line data.

**[P6, refuted] HKSS Claim A.4 as printed.** Take $d=87$ and $D=8700$. Exact counting gives

$$|N_{87,8700}|=sum_{j=0}^{100}{87j+2 choose2}=1,281,144,701.$$

The printed lower bound in Claim A.4 evaluates to

$$frac{D^3}{3d}-frac52D^2+frac{Dd}{6}=2,333,901,150,$$

which exceeds the exact count by $1,052,756,449$. Thus that claim is false as printed.

**[P7, proved] Repair of the coarse HKSS bound.** For general $d,D$, the decreasing function $(D-dx)^2$ gives

$$
|N_{d,D}|>=frac12 sum_{k=0}^{floor(D/d)}(D-dk)^2
>=frac12 int_0^{D/d}(D-dx)^2 dx
=frac{D^3}{6d}.
$$

Grouping positive $Z$-exponents into characteristic-length blocks shows that exponents divisible by the characteristic contribute at most a $1/p$ fraction of the monomials. Hence $|N_{d,D,p}|>=(1-1/p)|N_{d,D}|>=D^3/(12d)$ for $p>=2$. This repairs the coarse Claim A.6 without using the false Claim A.4.

**[P8, refuted] Instantiation of the printed KTZ slack chain.** At $r_0$,

$$87r_0=1,282,884,600,$$

and

$$35817^2=1,282,857,489<87r_0<1,282,929,124=35818^2.$$

Thus the KTZ choice is $16(35817+1)=573,088>p$. Exact counting lowers it to $87,668<p$, but later conditions still fail. For every $epsilon<=1$,

$$k_1=floor(epsilon p/1000)<=147,$$

so $D<k_1/2$ forces integer $D<=73$. Yet any polynomial with $A_Z ne0$ has weighted degree at least $87$. Also $384^2<p+1<385^2$, so

$$frac1{sqrt{p+1}}>frac1{385}>frac1{8000}>=frac{epsilon}{8000}.$$

Finally, the printed recovery $epsilon/8000$ is weaker than $epsilon/10$. Therefore the published explicit-slack chain cannot certify this instance, although this does not refute the asymptotic theorem.

**[P9, proved] Formal soundness at $epsilon_*=10^{-6}$.** For every $f:F_p^2 to F_p$, one value occurs at least $p$ times. The corresponding constant polynomial has total degree zero and agreement at least $1/p$. Since

$$frac1p>frac1{10,000,000}=frac{epsilon_*}{10},$$

the target conclusion holds whether or not the test passes. Thus $epsilon_*$ is a formally proved soundness value.

**[P10, proved] A point table with small degree-87 agreement.** There are at most $p^{3916}$ total-degree-at-most-87 bivariate polynomials. Choose $f$ uniformly and independently at every point. For fixed $Q$, let $X_Q$ be its number of agreements with $f$. Then $X_Q$ is binomial with parameters $p^2$ and $1/p$. Markov's inequality applied to $2^{X_Q}$ gives

$$Pr[X_Q>=2p]<=frac{(1+1/p)^{p^2}}{4^p}<left(frac{11}{16}right)^p.$$

Indeed, $(1+1/p)^p<e<11/4$; the latter follows from

$$e<=1+1+frac12+frac16+frac1{24}sum_{j>=0}4^{-j}=frac{49}{18}<frac{11}{4}.$$

Now $p<2^{18}$, $p=2*73,728+1$, and $(11/16)^2<1/2$. Therefore the union probability over all $Q$ is strictly below

$$p^{3916}(11/16)^p<2^{18*3916-73,728}=2^{-3240}<1.$$

Some deterministic $f$ consequently satisfies $Agr_{87}(f)<2/p$.

**[P11, proved] Adversarial line table.** On each affine line choose any 88 distinct points and interpolate their $f$-values by the unique univariate polynomial of degree at most 87. All Lagrange denominators are nonzero because $88<p$. Each line agrees at at least 88 points, so uniform line-then-point sampling gives

$$Pass(f,P)>=88/p.$$

Together with [P10], this refutes every $epsilon$ satisfying $20/p<=epsilon<=88/p$, because then $Pass>=epsilon$ while $Agr_{87}(f)<2/p<=epsilon/10$.

## Soundness Ledger

| Stage | Input | Exact loss | Output | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weighted monomial count | $r_0=14,745,800$, $D=87,668$ | At most $D+1=87,669$ conditions per line | Kernel dimension at least $20,520,648$ | proved |
| Family augmentation | $|R|<=r_0$ | No loss; added labels are discarded afterward | Lemma holds for every smaller family | proved |
| Derivative and cleanup | Nonzero kernel element | Weighted degree only decreases | Squarefree $A$, $A_Z ne0$, same line identities | proved |
| Formal target score | $Pass>=10^{-6}$ | Acceptance is completely discarded | $Agr_{87}>=1/p>10^{-7}=epsilon_*/10$ | proved |
| Exponential Markov bound | Fixed $Q$ | $Pr[X_Q>=2p]<(11/16)^p$ | Exact tail bound | proved |
| Union bound | At most $p^{3916}$ candidates | Total bad probability $<2^{-3240}$ | Existence of $f$ with $Agr_{87}<2/p$ | proved |
| Line interpolation | 88 chosen points on each line | No direction or averaging loss | $Pass>=88/p$ | proved |
| KTZ propagation | $epsilon<=1$ | Requires $D<=73$, although $A_Z ne0$ requires $D>=87$ | Printed fixed-constant chain is inapplicable | refuted |
| KTZ mixing | $epsilon<=1$ | $1/sqrt{p+1}>1/385>epsilon/8000$ | Printed mixing inequality is inapplicable | refuted |
| KTZ recovery | Surviving component | Factor $1/8000$ | Below the required factor $1/10$ | conditional/inadequate |

No Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, randomized numerical experiment, floating-point estimate, discriminant division, or unrecorded Markov loss occurs.

## Counterexample Attempts

1. **Concentrated directions.** The interpolation proof only needs distinct affine lines. A parallel family still supplies distinct irreducible linear factors, so concentration does not invalidate Lemma 1.

2. **Inseparability.** It cannot occur within the chosen weighted support: every positive $Z$-exponent is below the characteristic and $A_Z ne0$.

3. **Adversarial point and line tables.** Steps [P10]--[P11] give a rigorous construction by the probabilistic method. It uses the original uniform affine-line experiment and degree-87 line labels.

4. **Source-count stress test.** HKSS Claim A.4 fails by more than one billion monomials at the fixed specialization $d=87,D=8700$. The weaker bound actually needed for interpolation has a separate valid proof.

5. **Score monotonicity.** The target is true for every $epsilon<=10/p$ but false at $20/p$. Thus smaller epsilon is not stronger under the stated implication.

## Characteristic Audit

- The field is the stipulated prime field $F_{147457}$.
- $D=87,668<p$, so every restriction used here has formal degree below $p$.
- $deg_Z A<=1007<p$; positive exponents survive ordinary differentiation.
- Interpolation multiplicity is exactly one. No Hasse derivative or factorial is used.
- The adversarial Lagrange interpolation uses 88 distinct field elements, so every denominator is invertible.
- Squarefree cleanup does not divide by a derivative. It uses factorization only inside the UFD $F_p[X,Y,Z]$.
- No discriminant nonvanishing is claimed. The later KTZ generic-derivative/discriminant stage remains outside this result.
- Direction concentration is harmless, including a single parallel class.

## Limitations

This note does not prove a nonvacuous soundness theorem above the constant-polynomial floor. The reported $10^{-6}$ value is a formal benchmark improvement relative to the initial threshold $1$, but it demonstrates a defect in the objective rather than improved decoding.

The exact interpolation lemma covers the smallest KTZ-permitted selected-family size. KTZ Lemma 3.2 only provides a much larger upper bound, and its root-propagation budget is still incompatible with every nonzero-$Z$ interpolant at this field. New incidence sampling and cleanup constants are necessary.

The degree $87,668$ is optimal only for the universal coefficient-count certificate $N(D)>r_0(D+1)$. It is not a lower bound for structured line data.

All finite arithmetic is exposed above as integer sums and products, so no floating-point or unstored exhaustive computation is part of the proof. No files were modified. The active repository has no verifier audit, and this result has not undergone the two-verifier promotion process.
